items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1958-08-08; 1958-09-03
items.q: I played around here with Jelly Roll.

ctx.x: Oh, do you remember... No, you weren't here when Jelly Roll was out here, I guess, much.
At Leakes Lake. Sure. Where are you here? I played around here with Jelly Roll. That's right.
He was here then. You weren't here though when Buddy Petit and Frankie Dusen came out, were you?

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: Jolly Roll Morton played with us. We went there to play with Jolly Roll for two nights.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well, I was playing with Jolly Roll Morton's band. Yeah. Well, I was playing with Jolly Roll Morton's band. Oh, you played with Jolly Roll Morton's band? Yeah. Oh, you?

Well, I was playing myself, uh, everybody but, uh, Jolly Roll's band played. Jolly Roll Morton played with us. We went there to play with Jolly Roll for two nights. I see. He'd give a dance out to this place. Uh-huh. He'd run the place. He'd give dances out there all the time. Holidays and all sadness and Sundays. Yeah. And we went down to the play. So when they finished those two nights, Joe said, Well, we're going to New York. Who said that?

items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: Oh, he was rehearsing this band he had something for records and something else. I don't know. He had 12 of us.

ctx.x: Sounded like an orchestral idea. So did you work with him a little bit in the '40's?

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: Yeah. Yeah. We was gonna have an awful band. We had about ten or twelve of us.

ctx.x: Well that was Philip Kaiko was his brother. Cripple Pill. You remember Cripple Pill? I think he played banjo. No clarinet play. Yeah that was his brother and he was Kaiko. Yeah? Yeah. But I don't know and that's what Billy Moran's son, Lawrence Marrero used to call him Kaiko. Yeah. Did he ever play with Jelly Roll? Would you know? Who? Ernest Johnson. You wouldn't know maybe. Ernest was playing with the Black and Tanned. I don't think so now. Oh yeah. And what about Jelly Roll's band that he put up you know after…

Yeah. Yeah. We was gonna have an awful band. We had about ten or twelve of us. Let's see. Let's see. Let's see. I start the name. We had Buster Wilson on piano. Mmhmm. Buster Scott on guitar. I was on the bass. We had a... We had a... Mutt on trumpet. We had an Orion trombone. Mmhmm. Mmhmm.
